detail: bartcore_predictPerForest: this sampler reports no per-forest fits; only a coupling that composes its forests through scalar amplitude glue carries them
$getFitsWithoutOffset is not available on a multinomial sampler: its reported channels are per-category softmax probabilities rather than one additive location; $predict(data@x) serves that read
forest amplitudes require a sampler whose forests carry them
$setModel is not available on a multinomial sampler: every category forest's prior is calibrated at creation from the softmax map; make a new sampler instead
$setData is not available on a multinomial sampler: its K category forests fix their data at creation, and the count response is not a column of it; make a new sampler instead

$setResponse is not available on a multinomial sampler: its response is the n x K count matrix, which a flat vector cannot express and which a length-n integer vector would only be guessed into; replace it with $setCounts

$setOffset is not available on a multinomial sampler: a common per-observation shift is the softmax's own null direction, so a flat offset is inert; the shift that is not is the n x K matrix $setCategoryOffset takes
$setWeights is not available on a multinomial sampler: an integer case weight is already row-wise replication in its count response, and a non-integer one has no exact augmentation sampler
$setForestWeights is not available on a multinomial sampler: its forests are its categories, whose margin is a log-sum-exp over the other K - 1, so no forest carries a precision of its own
$setForestBasis is not available on a multinomial sampler: its forests are its categories, which carry no amplitudes and so no basis for any to multiply
$setSigma is not available on a multinomial sampler: the softmax carries no residual scale to set

bartcore_setTestOffset: a flat test offset is added to every reported channel after the categories are blended, which would move the reported probabilities off the simplex, and before the blend a common per-observation shift is inert; write an nTest x K matrix through the category test offset channel
$setCalibration is not available on a multinomial sampler: the softmax calibration map owns every category forest's leaf scale
